title: Audit logs & admin activity review with Constellation Finance
summary: Redwood walked Constellation through audit logging and admin activity: what fields are captured, export and SIEM integration options (S3, syslog, Kinesis, Kafka, BigQuery, ELK), retention defaults and paid long-term retention, and encryption/KMS options including customer-managed keys. Action items agreed: share SOC2/ISO summary, produce a 48h sample export, and confirm legal-hold needs.
topics: admin activity for RBAC/SSO/API keys/model changes
next_steps: Aisha to send SOC 2 & ISO summary + retention pricing (due: 2026-03-17)
Luca to run a 48h log export and share a redacted sample to Constellation (due: 2026-03-18)
Maya to confirm required retention window and legal-hold constraints (due: 2026-03-22)
Schedule technical deep-dive for SIEM integration if sample looks good (owner: Roberto)
action_items: Luca Moreno (Redwood): run 48h audit log export & share redacted sample (due: 2026-03-18)
Aisha Kumar (Redwood): share SOC 2 + ISO27001 summary and retention/pricing sheet (due: 2026-03-17)
Maya Patel (Constellation): confirm retention target and legal-hold process (due: 2026-03-22)
questions: Do audit logs include request/response payloads or only metadata?
Can we stream logs to our SIEM (Splunk) and keep a copy in our S3?
What retention options exist for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
How are keys managed and can we use CMKs/HSM?
Can logs be redacted for PII automatically?
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): ok everyone good afternoon, um thanks for joining. this is Aisha from Redwood and with me is Luca, our SE. today we wanted to run through audit logs and admin activity, specifically what we capture, how you can export it, retention and encryption options.
[00:18] Maya (Constellation): thanks, yeah we have a few folks on. I'm Maya, CISO, and interested in admin trails and legal hold. Roberto and Sofia are on too.
[00:26] Roberto (Constellation): hi all. quick ask: we use Splunk for our central logs, and we need near real-time streaming of admin events plus daily exports for retention.
[00:36] Luca (Redwood): great, that's common. at a high level our audit log capture covers actor, timestamp, action name, resource id/type, success/failure, source IP, user-agent, and request context. we also capture admin changes like role updates, SSO config changes, API key creation/deletion, and model/policy rollouts. there are optional bits like request payloads but we default to metadata-only for hosted customers unless you opt-in.
[01:02] Sofia (Constellation): when you say "request payloads", does that include prompts or embeddings? we can't keep raw prompts for compliance.
[01:08] Luca: good q. by default prompt payload storage is minimized — for hosted API we do not persist full prompt text in audit logs unless you enable full request logging for a specific integration. for Dedicated/Private you can choose to store or not store, and we support configurable masking/redaction rules (PII heuristics) and tokenization. note that redaction is best-effort at transcription time; we provide hooks to scrub before storage.
[01:36] Maya: ok, so for us we want metadata in logs and a separate controlled export for any payloads under legal hold.
[01:42] Aisha: that aligns with what our customers do. next, export paths — we support push and pull. push: syslog (TLS), HTTPS webhook, Kinesis/Kafka; pull: daily NDJSON exports to your S3 bucket or we can pop a signed URL for a range. SIEM connectors: native Splunk HEC integration, Elastic/ELK ingestion guide, and BigQuery sink via GCS.
[02:11] Roberto: format for S3 is ndjson per event? gzipped?
[02:15] Luca: yes ndjson, optionally gzipped and partitioned by date. you can choose fulldetail or minimal schema. sample exports include fields: event_id, ts, actor_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, ip, user_agent, request_hash, extra_meta. request_hash is a SHA256 of the payload so you can correlate without storing the raw payload.
[02:42] Maya: request_hash is useful. how about encryption at rest and KMS?
[02:45] Luca: logs are encrypted at rest. for hosted customers we manage keys by default; we also support CMK where you provide an AWS KMS key or bring-your-own-key via KMS or HSM for Private deployments. logs exported to your S3 can be encrypted with your bucket key. we also offer envelope encryption for extra layer.
[03:07] Sofia: do you provide attestations for key handling? we have internal auditors asking for HSM-backed CMKs.
[03:12] Aisha: we'll include the KMS/HSM section in the SOC 2 / ISO package we send. Redwood supports HSM-based key management for Private, and we have documented controls for key rotation and access auditing.
[03:26] Roberto: retention: default retention for hosted is what? 90 days?
[03:30] Luca: default hosted audit log retention is 90 days. Dedicated can be configured per contract — commonly 1 year or multi-year for compliance, and Private you set per your infra. we also offer extended retention as an add-on for hosted customers, with pricing per GB-month.
[03:47] Maya: for financials we need 7 years for some records, but probably only metadata. can you support legal-hold exports to cold storage?
[03:56] Luca: yes, we can support long-term cold export to your S3 Glacier or transfer to your long-term store. we do recommend exporting daily and validating checksums; we can automate lifecycle rules.
[04:06] Sofia: deletion workflows — if someone requests GDPR deletion, how do you handle traces in logs?
[04:11] Luca: good one. logs are immutable once written, so PII should be redacted before logging. for GDPR deletion we can delete records from our active store and, for exports you control (your S3), it's your bucket policy. we also support log redaction and on-request purging in Private setups where you control storage.
[04:30] Maya: curious about admin activity detail level: will audit logs show the old and new role when someone changes RBAC?
[04:36] Luca: yes, role change events include before/after metadata for role assignments, plus who performed the change and via which method (console, API, SSO). we also log SSO assertions and session IDs to help trace authentications.
[04:50] Roberto: what about API key usage — do you log each API key id on every request?
[04:54] Luca: we log key id and truncated key fingerprint; full key values are never stored in logs. we also provide rate/volume metrics by key and can stream aggregated metrics to your monitoring stack.
[05:07] Aisha: note that for compliance customers we can enable certificate-based auth and rotate keys via our API.
[05:12] Speaker 1 (Constellation): there's sometimes a mismatch in transcribed product names — "Redwood Dedicated" gets written wrong in our docs as "Redwood Dedicate" — not important but just FYI.
[05:20] Luca: ha, we see that. okay back to connectors — we also support webhook delivery with retries and dead-letter queues if the endpoint is down, and batching to control throughput/costs.
[05:34] Maya: can we filter which events stream to Splunk? we don't want noise, just admin and security-relevant events.
[05:40] Luca: yes filters by event type, resource, or actor are supported; you can create routes so only admin-level events are sent to SIEM while application events can be stored in separate buckets.
[05:50] Sofia: are there any throttling or sampling policies that would drop events we need?
[05:54] Luca: we do have backpressure policies for extreme bursts; standard admin events are low-volume and not sampled. for high-volume telemetry we may sample but sampling is configurable and we can disable sampling for tagged events.
[06:06] Roberto: question on integrity — how do we prove logs haven't been tampered with?
[06:10] Luca: we provide signed manifests and optional cryptographic chaining for exports (like signing each file and providing manifests with checksums). for Dedicated/Private you can also enable WORM-like policies in your storage.
[06:23] Maya: ok good. can you show an example event?
[06:26] Luca: (reads) { event_id: "evt-...", ts: "2026-03-15T14:12:03Z", actor_id: "u-1234", actor_email: "m.patel@constellation.com", action: "role.assign", resource_type: "org.user", resource_id: "u-5678", before: "viewer", after: "admin", outcome: "success", ip: "34.22.10.12" } — in the actual export before/after are redacted if requested and large payloads are replaced with hashes.
[07:00] Maya: that's exactly what we need. about access to audit logs inside Redwood console: who can see them?
[07:05] Luca: RBAC applies — only roles with the "audit:read" permission can view logs in the console. we also record access to audit logs themselves. so viewing logs generates an access event that is logged.
[07:18] Sofia: SSO and session length — do you log session creations and token refreshes?
[07:22] Luca: yes session start/refresh/terminate events are logged with assertion IDs, provider name, and user id.
[07:29] Aisha: for integrations and next steps we'll prepare a sample export and the SOC2/ISO pack. Luca, can you run the export for Constellation and redact sensitive fields?
[07:38] Luca: yeah I'll run a 48 hour export, redact PII and ship a gzipped ndjson sample to their review bucket. I'll also include a schema doc.
[07:46] Roberto: perfect. also share your pricing for extended retention.
[07:49] Aisha: will do. anything else on encryption or residency?
[07:52] Maya: residency — we need EU region for EU customers. do you have regional log storage?
[07:58] Luca: yes, we support region-specific retention and storage; for hosted we have EU and US regions, Dedicated can be deployed to whichever region you contract, and Private obviously sits in your network. we'll note region in the sample metadata.
[08:12] Sofia: tiny pedantic note: the transcript sometimes says "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" — i've seen that in other meetings.
[08:18] Aisha: noted. okay to recap: Redwood provides metadata-first audit logs (optional full payloads), multiple export paths (S3/NDJSON, syslog, SIEM connectors, Kinesis/Kafka), default 90d retention for hosted with paid extended options, CMK/HSM support, PII redaction and legal-hold exports, and RBAC on log access. next steps are in the action items.
[08:42] Maya: thanks, schedule the deep dive once we review the sample.
[08:46] Aisha: thanks everyone. we'll follow up by EOD with the SOC2 packet and schedule options.
[08:51] (meeting ends)
